---
title: "Live polls for Quarto revealjs"
subtitle: "Polls and word clouds over a seminar socket.io server"
format:
  revealjs:
    revealjs-plugins:
      - livepoll
filters:
  - livepoll
# Top level, not under `format:`: the filter reads it to configure poll.html.
seminar:
  server: "http://localhost:8080/"
  url: "seminar-quarto-demo"   # the venue
  room: "demo"
  # bcrypt hash of the host password. Replace it with your own (see README):
  # with this placeholder the deck renders and runs, but hosting is refused.
  hash: "$2a$05$REPLACE.THIS.WITH.YOUR.OWN.BCRYPT.HASH.SEE.README.."
livepoll:
  layout: embedded             # classic | embedded; per question with layout="..."
  quiz: true                   # nicknames, points and the leaderboard slide
  # signals: true             # "Lost me" / "Slow down" buttons on the phones
  # reactions: true            # emoji reactions that float up the slide
---

## Join in

Scan to open the poll page, or press **Shift+Q** for a full-screen QR code.

::: {.poll-qr size="300"}
:::

::: {.notes}
Open the menu (bottom left, or Shift+L), go to the **Live poll** tab, enter
the password and press Start.
:::

## Which language do you use most?

::: {.poll #lang}
- R
- Python
- Julia
- Something else
:::

## What is the capital of Australia?

::: {.poll #capital}
- [ ] Sydney
- [x] Canberra
- [ ] Melbourne
- [ ] Perth
:::

::: {.notes}
Press space to reveal the answer: the correct row turns green, and the phones
show it too.
:::

## Before the reveal

::: {.poll #pvalue results="hidden"}
A p-value of 0.03 means:

- [ ] There is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true
- [x] Data this extreme would occur 3% of the time if the null were true
- [ ] There is a 97% chance the result is real
:::

## Pick every prime

::: {.poll #primes max-choices="3"}
- [x] 2
- [x] 3
- [ ] 9
- [x] 11
:::

::: {.notes}
Several choices: phones get toggles and a Submit button, and the bars show
the share of people who picked each one.
:::

## Peer instruction

::: {.poll #ci rounds="2" timer="60"}
A 95% confidence interval for a mean is (4.1, 5.3). Which is right?

- [ ] There is a 95% chance the true mean is in (4.1, 5.3)
- [x] 95% of intervals built this way contain the true mean
- [ ] 95% of the data lie in (4.1, 5.3)
:::

::: {.notes}
Vote, talk to your neighbour, vote again. The timer runs for a minute and
then moves on to round 2 by itself (or press space). Round 2's bars show where
round 1 was; after it, space reveals the answer. Shift+T pauses the timer.
:::

## How many?

::: {.estimate #beans min="0" max="1000" answer="412" tolerance="10%"}
How many jelly beans are in the jar?
:::

## What should we revisit?

::: {.rank #revisit top="3"}
Put your top three in order.

- Sampling distributions
- Confidence intervals
- Hypothesis tests
- Power
- Regression
:::

## Spot the outlier

::: {.hotspot #outlier answer="0.75,0.80,0.05"}
Tap the point that does not fit.

![](images/scatter.svg)
:::

## Draw your guess

::: {.sketch #rt x="20,80" y="200,600" x-label="Age" y-label="Reaction time (ms)" answer="20:250, 40:280, 60:340, 80:450"}
How does reaction time change with age?
:::

::: {.notes}
Phones draw a curve; the slide shows every curve, the class median and the
middle half. Space reveals the real data (dashed).
:::

## One word for today?

::: {.wordcloud #today max-words="2"}
:::

## How was the pace?

## Your questions

::: {.qa}
:::

Questions come in all session from the poll page's Questions tab, and people
